name: bridge driver
description: Default Docker network driver. Creates an in-kernel Linux bridge (default `docker0`) plus per-container veth pairs. IPv4 subnet (and optional IPv6 subnet); per-container interface in that subnet; embedded DNS for user-defined bridges (containers reach each other by name). User-defined bridges > the default bridge: scoped isolation, automatic name DNS, configurable per-network, attach/detach on the fly. Docker manages an `iptables` (or `nftables`) ruleset for NAT/masquerade/ICC.

name: host driver
description: Removes network isolation between container and host: container shares the host's network namespace. No port mapping needed; container can `bind 0.0.0.0:80` directly to the host's interfaces. No iptables rules created for host networking. Linux-only; on Docker Desktop runs through the VM. Use for ultra-low-latency or when port-mapping overhead is intolerable.

name: overlay driver
description: Multi-host network across Swarm members. VXLAN tunnel (default UDP 4789) carries traffic between hosts. Required for Swarm services or for standalone containers that need to talk across hosts (`--attachable`). Optional `--opt encrypted` enables IPsec at the VXLAN layer (non-trivial perf cost; not supported for Windows containers). Required ports between hosts: 2377/tcp (control plane), 4789/udp (data), 7946/tcp+udp (gossip).

name: ipvlan driver
description: L2 or L3 network virtualization on top of a parent host interface (no Linux bridge in between). Lighter than bridge; container interfaces attach directly to the host NIC's L2 / L3 path. `-o parent=eth0` selects the parent. Containers cannot ping the host on the same parent (kernel filter). No port-publishing needed in L2 (containers get routable IPs).

name: ipvlan L3 mode
description: Routed (L3) variant of ipvlan. The host acts as a router between container subnets. Container traffic is forwarded by the host's routing table; no broadcast/multicast leaks across `parent` interfaces. Different containers can sit on different L3 subnets sharing one parent. Useful when you want isolated L3 segments without L2 exposure.

name: macvlan driver
description: Each container gets a unique MAC address on the host's physical network — appears as a fully separate device to the LAN. Modes: bridge (default), private, vepa, passthru. Requires the host NIC to allow promiscuous mode (or many MACs); cloud providers often disallow. Best for legacy apps that expect to be directly on the LAN.

name: none driver
description: Container has only `lo` — no other network interface, no internet, no DNS. Used for batch/CPU jobs that mustn't reach the network, or as a base for hand-crafted netns wiring. `docker run --network=none …`. Detail in `docker-docs-network-none`.

name: docker network (object)
description: A Docker-managed network — driver name + scope + subnet(s) + gateway + IPAM config + per-network options. Listed by `docker network ls`; created by `docker network create`. From the engine, just an attachment endpoint; from the networking leaf, the concrete on-host construct (a Linux bridge, an overlay VXLAN, a parent-attached ipvlan).

name: default bridge (`bridge`)
description: The bridge network Docker auto-creates: name `bridge`, host interface `docker0`. Containers without `--network` join it. Configurable only via `daemon.json` (bip, mtu, fixed-cidr, ip-masq, icc) — needs daemon restart. Considered legacy; prefer user-defined bridges. Lacks DNS-by-name (containers must be `--link`'d to resolve by name).

name: user-defined bridge
description: A bridge created via `docker network create -d bridge <name>`. Embedded DNS (containers resolve each other by name/alias). Configurable per-network. Containers can be attached/detached on the fly via `docker network connect/disconnect`. Effectively all-ports-open between same-network containers; need explicit `--publish` for outside reach.

name: network endpoint
description: A container's attachment to one network — its veth pair, IP, MAC, aliases. A container can have N endpoints (N networks). Surfaced as `NetworkSettings.Networks.<name>` in `docker inspect`. Each endpoint has its own IPAddress, Gateway, MacAddress, Aliases.

name: embedded DNS resolver
description: Per-bridge in-kernel DNS server at 127.0.0.11 in user-defined bridges. Resolves container names and aliases on the network; falls back to host's resolver for everything else. The mechanism behind `db` resolving to the db container's IP from the web container.

name: port binding
description: A daemon-managed mapping `hostIP:hostPort -> containerIP:containerPort/proto`. Created by `-p`/`--publish`/`-P`. Implemented as DNAT in iptables (or nftables) plus userland-proxy for loopback. Visible in `docker port` and `docker inspect`'s NetworkSettings.Ports.

name: PortMap record
description: The `HostConfig.PortBindings` and `NetworkSettings.Ports` shape: a JSON object keyed by `<port>/<proto>`, value is an array of {HostIp, HostPort}. Empty array = all interfaces, ephemeral host port. The structural representation of a port binding.

name: published port
description: A container port that's been opened to outside-the-container clients via `-p`. Distinct from EXPOSE (which is just metadata). Format `[hostIP:][hostPort]:containerPort[/proto]`; missing hostPort = random ephemeral port; missing hostIP = all interfaces.

name: host port
description: The host-side port a published port lands on. With `-P` (`--publish-all`), each EXPOSE'd port gets a random high port from the ephemeral range. Inspect with `docker port <container>` or `docker ps`'s PORTS column.

name: container IP
description: The per-endpoint IP assigned to a container on a network. Comes from the network's IPAM pool by default; pin with `docker network connect --ip <addr>` or `docker run --ip <addr>` (only works on user-defined networks with `--subnet`).

name: gateway IP
description: The network's gateway address — typically `.1` of the subnet. The container's default route. For bridge networks, this is also the host's interface IP on the bridge (containers reach the host via this address).

name: IPAM pool
description: A {subnet, ip-range?, gateway, aux-addresses} tuple defining the IP space a network can hand out. One pool per IPv4/IPv6 leg per network. Daemon-wide pool defaults via `default-address-pools`; per-network override via `--subnet/--ip-range/--gateway/--aux-address` on `docker network create`.

name: iptables nat table
description: Where Docker installs PREROUTING/OUTPUT/POSTROUTING rules for port-publish DNAT and bridge SNAT (masquerade). `iptables -t nat -L -n -v` shows them. The table where `-p 80:80` becomes a DNAT to the container's 172.x.0.x:80.

name: iptables filter table
description: Where Docker installs FORWARD chain rules to enforce inter-network isolation and let port-published traffic through. The table that drops cross-bridge traffic by default unless explicitly accepted via DOCKER-USER.

name: iptables mangle table
description: Used by Swarm routing mesh and by `bridge-accept-fwmark` to handle marked packets. Less common in single-host Docker but visible on swarm nodes.

name: DOCKER chain
description: Custom chain in `nat` and `filter` tables Docker manages for port-publish DNAT and bridge filter rules. Append-only by Docker itself; user rules don't go here. Inspect: `iptables -t nat -L DOCKER -n`.

name: DOCKER-USER chain
description: User-editable chain in the `filter` table, traversed BEFORE DOCKER. Only place you can safely add rules that affect Docker traffic without Docker overwriting them. e.g. drop external-source packets to specific published ports.

name: DOCKER-ISOLATION-STAGE-1 chain
description: Filter-table chain that drops packets between different bridge networks. Stage 1 matches input bridge; stage 2 matches output bridge. Together they enforce per-bridge isolation.

name: DOCKER-ISOLATION-STAGE-2 chain
description: Filter-table chain paired with STAGE-1 to enforce inter-bridge isolation. Drops if output bridge differs from input bridge for FORWARD-ed packets.

name: nftables table (docker)
description: Modern alternative to iptables. Selectable via daemon `firewall-backend: nftables`. Same logical rule set; uses single nftables table with chains for prerouting/postrouting/forward/output. Different toolchain (`nft list ruleset`).

name: Linux bridge (host-side)
description: The kernel software bridge that bridge-driver builds on. Default `docker0`; user-defined networks get bridges named like `br-<network-id-prefix>`. Inspectable with `ip link show type bridge`, `bridge link show`, `brctl show`. Containers' veth ends are slaved to this bridge.

name: veth pair
description: Linux virtual ethernet pair: two interfaces, packets out one come in the other. Per container endpoint Docker creates one veth pair: container side moved into the container's netns (named `eth0` typically); host side stays in the root netns slaved to the bridge.

name: network namespace (runtime)
description: Each container endpoint lives in a network namespace (its own routing table, iptables rules, interfaces). For bridge networks, container netns contains the eth0 (one end of the veth) + lo. Inspect with `nsenter --net --target <pid>` or `ip netns list`.

name: VXLAN tunnel
description: L2-over-UDP encapsulation used by overlay networks. Default UDP port 4789. Each overlay's traffic carries its VNI (VXLAN Network Identifier). Inspect on the host with `ip -d link show vxlan0`.

name: sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward
description: Kernel sysctl that enables IP forwarding (host acts as router between interfaces). Docker auto-enables on dockerd start (and also `net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding`). When Docker enables it, it also installs a default-DROP FORWARD policy unless `ip-forward-no-drop` is set. Critical: disabling kills all bridge-network outbound.

name: userland proxy
description: Per-published-port `docker-proxy` process bridging hairpin/loopback traffic that NAT can't handle (e.g. container hitting its own published port from the host's loopback). Toggleable via `--userland-proxy=false`. Disabling pushes work into iptables but breaks some odd cases. The reason `ps -ef | grep docker-proxy` shows one process per published port.

name: port publish host-binding
description: Default behavior of `-p 80` / `-p 8080:80` — bind the published port to ALL host addresses (0.0.0.0 and ::). Override per-network via `com.docker.network.bridge.host_binding_ipv4` or per-port via `-p 127.0.0.1:8080:80`.

name: port publish — explicit host IP
description: `-p <host-ip>:<host-port>:<container-port>[/proto]`. Restricts publish to a specific host IP. Common pattern: `-p 127.0.0.1:5432:5432` to expose Postgres only to local clients on the host.

name: embedded DNS feature
description: Daemon-side DNS server at 127.0.0.11 inside containers on user-defined bridges/overlays. Resolves container names + aliases; forwards everything else to the host's resolvers. Disable per-container with `--dns` to provide custom servers.

name: network alias
description: Additional hostname for a container on a network. Set via `--network-alias <name>` or `docker network connect --alias`. Useful for blue/green or canary patterns where multiple containers should resolve at the same name.

name: multi-network attach
description: A single container can be attached to N networks. Done either at create time (`--network` repeatable) or after start with `docker network connect`. Each attach creates a new endpoint with its own IP; routing inside the container picks the appropriate interface per destination subnet.

name: overlay encryption
description: `--opt encrypted` on `docker network create -d overlay` — IPsec at the VXLAN layer. Non-trivial CPU cost; not supported on Windows containers. Use only when host-to-host links are untrusted.

name: swarm routing mesh
description: Swarm-built ingress overlay network: `docker service create --publish` exposes a port on every Swarm node, routing requests to a healthy task replica anywhere. Implemented as a special `ingress` network created automatically; uses iptables marks + IPVS.

name: legacy `--link`
description: Deprecated. On the default bridge, `--link source:alias` injects /etc/hosts entries and shares env vars. User-defined bridges' DNS-by-name supersedes this; `--link` is preserved for the default bridge only.

name: IPv6 on bridge
description: Per-network `--ipv6` enables a v6 subnet (auto-pick a ULA, or `--subnet 2001:db8::/64`). Daemon-wide `ipv6: true` + `fixed-cidr-v6` for the default bridge. ip6tables rules managed by Docker (toggle via `ip6tables: true` / `--ip6tables=false`).

name: network MTU
description: Per-network MTU set via `-o com.docker.network.driver.mtu` or daemon-wide `--mtu`. Default 1500. Lower (1450) on hosts behind GRE/IPsec/VXLAN tunnels — without this, large packets are silently dropped by the encap path. Symptom: small TCP flows work, large writes hang.

name: subnet (CIDR)
description: `--subnet <CIDR>` defines the address space a network's containers draw from. One IPv4 + one IPv6 subnet per network max. CIDR collisions with on-prem subnets break routing — pin with `default-address-pools` to avoid surprises.

name: IP range
description: `--ip-range <CIDR>` carves out a sub-range of `--subnet` from which Docker auto-assigns container IPs. Containers can still be statically pinned outside the range (via `--ip`).

name: IPAM driver
description: The IP-address-management plugin a network uses (`default` is built-in). Pluggable for vendor IPAM (e.g. Calico's IPAM). Configured via `--ipam-driver` + `--ipam-opt` on `docker network create`.

name: IPAM config
description: The {subnet, ip-range, gateway, aux-addresses} bundle a network commits to. Surfaced as `IPAM.Config[]` in `docker network inspect`.

name: default-address-pools
description: Daemon-level `default-address-pools` controls which IP ranges get sliced into per-user-defined-network subnets. e.g. `[{base: 10.10.0.0/16, size: 24}]` carves out /24s from 10.10.0.0/16. CRITICAL when on-prem ranges collide with default 172.17–172.31 / 192.168.x.x picks.

name: NAT / SNAT for containers
description: Bridge driver SNATs container-originated traffic to the host's IP via iptables MASQUERADE in POSTROUTING. Toggleable per-network via `com.docker.network.bridge.enable_ip_masquerade` or daemon-wide via `--ip-masq`. Disabling = container packets keep internal IP, often filtered by external networks.

name: docker0 interface
description: The default-bridge's host-side interface. `ip addr show docker0` shows it; default IPv4 = first /16 not colliding (172.17.0.1/16). Renaming/customizing requires daemon restart with `--bridge` flag (rare).

name: proxy ARP
description: Kernel feature where one host answers ARP for IPs that don't live on its interfaces. Used by ipvlan-l3 + macvlan setups so the upstream router can reach container IPs on the parent interface. `sysctl net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.proxy_arp=1`.

name: ARP table
description: Per-netns mapping of IP→MAC. `ip neigh` (or `arp -an`) inside a container's netns shows it. Stale entries cause ~3s pauses on inter-container connect; `gc_thresh*` sysctls tune kernel cache. Helpful debug step on flaky bridge networks.

name: routing table
description: Per-netns route table. `ip route` inside a container; multi-network containers have one route per attached subnet plus a default via the gateway of the first network. `ip rule` for policy routing.

name: conntrack
description: Kernel connection-tracking subsystem. Docker's NAT depends on it. `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` to see live entries; bumping `nf_conntrack_max` is the fix for 'nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet' on heavy port-published hosts.

name: port conflict
description: `Bind for 0.0.0.0:80 failed: port is already allocated`. Caused by another process (or another container) holding the host port. Diagnose: `ss -tlnp | grep :80`, `docker ps --filter publish=80`. Fix: stop the holder, or pick a different host port.

name: `docker port` shortcut
description: `docker port <container> [<port>[/<proto>]]` reads back the live `hostIP:hostPort` for a published container port. Useful when `-P` was used (port is randomized).
